question: A bathroom floor measures 3.5 m in length and 2 m in width. One of its walls, which is to be tiled fully, measures 2 m in length and 2.5 m in height. If square tiles of side 25 cm are used, and an extra 12% of tiles are purchased to cover cuts and wastage, how many tiles are needed in total?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of the wall to be tiled = 2 m × 2.5 m = 5 m² = 50000 cm².

Area of 1 square tile = 25 cm × 25 cm = 625 cm².

Base number of tiles needed = 50000 ÷ 625 = 80 tiles.

Total tiles including 12% extra wastage = 80 × 1.12 = 89.6 tiles.

Since tiles can only be purchased in whole numbers, round up to 90.

**∴ The correct answer is 90 tiles.**
